correctness.rationale: Every state is generated exactly from all \(2^{16}\) horizontal assignments and exact vertical recursion; no possible configuration is omitted. For every move, the toggled state passes all ice constraints exactly iff the given simple cycle is coherently directed. A union–find census of all 2970 states and all 256 specified move repertoires proves 19/11/1 component counts and 225 connected cases. A separately formulated Gray-coded \(Q_4\) edge-orientation enumeration with independent adjacency calculation reproduces every classification. Flux invariance proves necessity; finite connectivity and monotonicity establish sufficiency. The result does not extrapolate past the 4-by-4 graph.

value.rationale: The physical square-ice torus has topologically protected winding sectors, creating a direct obstacle to local Markov-chain sampling. The precise minimal predetermined nonlocal update repertoire is a natural operational invariant: just one fixed row and one fixed column cycle, together with all plaquettes, make the entire 2970-state system irreducible, while either kind alone provably fails. The sharp 16 minimal pairs and complete 225/256 classification provide a reproducible finite benchmarking fact not furnished by the known face-only census. No general-size or mixing-speed contribution is asserted.
